subject: Leaf scavenger hunt, Tyke Hikes and a Frozen movie night
preheader: Plus: Memorial Park's new Camp Logan Playground is under construction.
intro: Halloween is behind us, and the next two weeks are quiet in the best way. Saturday afternoon, the Arboretum has a free fall-leaf scavenger hunt on the trails, and Tyke Hikes start up again Monday for your 18-months-to-4 crowd.

Two heads-ups: clocks went back this weekend, so expect early wake-ups for a few days, and Hatchlings baby classes at the Arboretum are sold out this fall. Looking ahead, put Friday, Dec 4 on the calendar for a free Frozen movie night in Memorial Park.

items.title: Memorial Park's new Camp Logan Playground is under construction
items.description: Part of the 100-acre Memorial Groves project, the new playground will have giant helmets, army crates and even a huge loaf of bread to climb, inspired by the park's WWI history. A visitor center, restrooms and trails are coming too. Completion is targeted for late 2027.
paragraphs: Part of the 100-acre Memorial Groves project, the new playground will have giant helmets, army crates and even a huge loaf of bread to climb, inspired by the park's WWI history. A visitor center, restrooms and trails are coming too. Completion is targeted for late 2027.

image.alt: Illustration: Kids (ages 4–10) with clipboards and crayons on a forest trail, holding up colorful fall leaves to match a scavenger-hunt sheet, parents walking behind

items.title: Fall Foliage scavenger hunt
items.description: A free, self-guided scavenger hunt on the trails about fall leaves, any time between 2 and 4 pm. Start at the Nature Center. All ages; wear closed-toe shoes and bring water and bug spray.

image.alt: Illustration: A naturalist leads toddlers and preschoolers with parents along a shady woodland trail, kids pointing at leaves and a pond, strollers on the path

items.title: Tyke Hikes en español
items.description: A Spanish-language nature walk for ages 18 months to 4 with a grown-up: a story, a sensory activity and a stroller-friendly hike. Younger siblings welcome. Parking is $6.50.

items.title: Tyke Hike at Arrowwood Pond
items.when: Select Mondays: Nov 2, 9, 16, then Dec 7, 14, 21 · 9:30 am–10:15 am
items.description: A naturalist leads a story, a simple nature activity and a stroller-friendly trail hike for ages 18 months to 4 with a grown-up. Two sessions, 9:30 and 10:30 am.

items.title: Stories & Crafts in the Cabin
items.description: A nature story and craft in the sanctuary's log cabin for ages 3–5 with an adult. Siblings with a supervising adult come free.

items.title: Hatchlings outdoor play for babies
items.cost: $12 members / $15 nonmembers per child and caregiver
items.description: **Registration is full** for 2026 classes; check for a waitlist. Messy outdoor play with sand, mud, sticks and leaves for ages 0–18 months with a caregiver. Bring a change of clothes.

items.title: Baby Bouncers playtime
items.description: Bouncy songs, rhymes and playtime for crawlers and babies taking their first steps. Two sessions, 10:15 and 11:15.

items.title: Toddler storytime
items.description: Books, songs and movement for ages 18–36 months with a caregiver.

items.title: Tiny Tykes storytime
items.description: Interactive storytime for new walkers and their grown-ups: stories, songs and finger plays. Two sessions, 10:15 and 11:15. Some weeks it's outside in the Reading Garden.

items.title: Ciro's Italian Grill
items.description: Family-owned Italian spot with a two-story space, wood-fired pizza, a gelato bar and a patio with room for kids to play.

items.title: Lupe Tortilla
items.description: Tex-Mex with an outdoor play area, a Houston family favorite for fajita night.

items.title: The Decoy
items.when: Spring Branch · $$ · Patio, Lawn to run
items.description: A family- and pet-friendly sand volleyball spot with three courts, cornhole and yard games. Best for an easy early dinner while kids play in the sand.

image.alt: Illustration: A warm, realistic, candid photo in a Houston driveway on a cool, bright winter morning, landscape

items.title: That puffy coat makes the car seat feel safer. It isn't.
items.description: Why winter coats and car-seat straps don't mix, the 30-second test to check any jacket, and cozy ways to keep little ones warm on cold Houston mornings and holiday road trips.

image.alt: Illustration: A toddler in dinosaur pajamas sits cross-legged on a rug, chin in hand, watching a tablet propped against a cushion

items.title: Screen-time guilt? The research is kinder than you think.
items.description: What pediatricians actually recommend for babies through age 6, why what they watch beats how long, and simple ways to make screen time calmer (meltdown included).

items.title: SBISD Thanksgiving break
items.description: No school all week. Plan library visits and park days early, since popular spots fill up.
